 27: @export var light_level: float = 0.0  # 0.0 = dim, 1.0 = bright (affects ambiance)
 28: @export var atmosphere_tags: Array[String] = []  # ["cozy", "professional", "creative"]
 29: 
 30: # Program & Service Integration
 31: @export var supports_program_types: Array[String] = []  # ["story_time", "study_group"]
 32: @export var supports_service_types: Array[String] = []  # ["cafe", "printing"]
 33: @export var is_program_fixture: bool = false  # Required for specific programs
 34: @export var is_service_fixture: bool = false  # Required for specific services
 35: 
 36: # Unlock Conditions
 37: @export var unlock_requirements: Dictionary = {}  # Same structure as ProgramDefinition
 38: 
 39: # Theme & Aesthetics (for future use)
 40: @export var style_category: String = "standard"  # "standard", "vintage", "modern", "luxury"
 41: @export var color_variant: String = "default"
 42: 
 43: # Maintenance
 44: @export var repair_cost: int = 0  # Cost to repair when damaged
 45: @export var replacement_cost: int = 0  # Cost to replace (usually = purchase_price)
 46: 
 47: # ============================================================================
 48: # COMPUTED PROPERTIES
 49: # ============================================================================
 50: 
 51: func get_current_condition() -> float:
 52: 	"""Returns current condition as percentage (0.0 to 1.0)"""
 53: 	return durability / 100.0
 54: 
 55: func is_damaged() -> bool:
 56: 	"""Returns true if durability below 30%"""
 57: 	return durability < 30
 58: 
 59: func needs_repair() -> bool:
 60: 	"""Returns true if durability below 70%"""
 61: 	return durability < 70
 62: 
 63: func get_effective_comfort() -> float:
 64: 	"""Returns comfort rating adjusted by condition"""
 65: 	return comfort_rating * get_current_condition()
 66: 
 67: func get_effective_prestige() -> float:
 68: 	"""Returns prestige contribution adjusted by condition"""
 69: 	return prestige_contribution * get_current_condition()
 70: 
 71: func apply_wear(amount: int = 1):
 72: 	"""Apply wear and tear from normal use"""
 73: 	durability = max(0, durability - amount)
 74: 
 75: func apply_damage(amount: int):
 76: 	"""Apply damage from ghost attacks"""
 77: 	durability = max(0, durability - amount)
 78: 
 79: func repair(amount: int = 100):
 80: 	"""Repair item up to max durability"""
 81: 	durability = min(100, durability + amount)
 82: 
 83: func full_repair():
 84: 	"""Restore to perfect condition"""
 85: 	durability = 100
 86: 
 87: # ============================================================================
 88: # VALIDATION
 89: # ============================================================================
 90: 
 91: func can_support_program(program_id: String) -> bool:
 92: 	"""Check if this furniture can support a specific program"""
 93: 	return program_id in supports_program_types
 94: 
 95: func can_support_service(service_id: String) -> bool:
 96: 	"""Check if this furniture can support a specific service"""
 97: 	return service_id in supports_service_types
 98: 
 99: func is_suitable_for_activity(activity: String) -> bool:
100: 	"""Check if this furniture supports a guest activity"""
101: 	return supports_activity == activity or activity in supports_program_types
102: 
103: # ============================================================================
104: # DESCRIPTION HELPERS
105: # ============================================================================
106: 
107: func get_detailed_description() -> String:
108: 	"""Returns full description with stats"""
109: 	var desc = description + "\n\n"
110: 	
111: 	if comfort_rating > 0:
112: 		desc += "Comfort: %d/10\n" % int(comfort_rating * 10)
113: 	
114: 	if prestige_contribution > 0:
115: 		desc += "Prestige: +%.1f\n" % prestige_contribution
116: 	
117: 	if guest_capacity > 1:
118: 		desc += "Capacity: %d guests\n" % guest_capacity
119: 	
120: 	if supports_activity != "":
121: 		desc += "Activity: %s\n" % supports_activity
122: 	
123: 	if atmosphere_tags.size() > 0:
124: 		desc += "Atmosphere: %s\n" % ", ".join(atmosphere_tags)
125: 	
126: 	return desc
127: 
128: func get_condition_text() -> String:
129: 	"""Returns text description of current condition"""
130: 	var condition = get_current_condition()
131: 	if condition >= 0.9:
132: 		return "Excellent"
133: 	elif condition >= 0.7:
134: 		return "Good"
135: 	elif condition >= 0.5:
136: 		return "Fair"
137: 	elif condition >= 0.3:
138: 		return "Poor"
139: 	else:
140: 		return "Damaged"
</file>

<file path="IncursionState.gd">
  1: extends Node
  2: 
  3: ## Global state tracker for all Ghost Incursions
  4: ## Persists completion status, player choices, and discovered lore
  5: ## Autoload as "IncursionState"
  6: 
  7: # ============================================================================
  8: # ACTIVE INCURSIONS
  9: # ============================================================================
 10: 
 11: # Currently active incursion per room
 12: var active_incursions: Dictionary = {}  # room_id -> IncursionDefinition
 13: 
 14: # ============================================================================
 15: # COMPLETION TRACKING
 16: # ============================================================================
 17: 
 18: var completed_incursions: Dictionary = {}  # incursion_id -> completion_data
 19: # completion_data structure:
 20: # {
 21: #   "completed_day": int,
 22: #   "resolution_type": String ("banishment", "release", "partial"),
 23: #   "time_taken": float,
 24: #   "clues_found": int,
 25: #   "combat_used": bool
 26: # }
 27: 
 28: # ============================================================================
 29: # DISCOVERED CLUES
 30: # ============================================================================
 31: 
 32: var discovered_clues: Dictionary = {}  # incursion_id -> Array[int] (clue indices)
 33: 
 34: # ============================================================================
 35: # COLLECTIBLES
 36: # ============================================================================
 37: 
 38: var collected_anchor_objects: Array[String] = []  # object_ids preserved
 39: 
 40: # ============================================================================
 41: # LIFECYCLE METHODS
 42: # ============================================================================
 43: 
 44: func _ready():
 45: 	Signals.subscribe("game.night.started", _on_night_started, self)
 46: 	Signals.subscribe("game.night.ended", _on_night_ended, self)
 47: 	Signals.subscribe("estate.room_cleared", _on_room_cleared, self)
 48: 
 49: func _on_night_started(_payload: Dictionary):
 50: 	# Spawn active incursions for unlocked, uncleared rooms
 51: 	# WARN: IncursionManager calls this now, need to resequence autoloads
 52: 	# load_active_incursions()
 53: 	print("Active incursions: ", IncursionState.active_incursions.keys())
 54: 
 55: func _on_night_ended(_payload: Dictionary):
 56: 	# Clean up any temporary state
 57: 	pass
 58: 
 59: func _on_room_cleared(payload: Dictionary):
 60: 	var room_id = payload.get("room_id", "")
 61: 	if active_incursions.has(room_id):
 62: 		active_incursions.erase(room_id)
 63: 
 64: # ============================================================================
 65: # INCURSION ACTIVATION
 66: # ============================================================================
 67: 
 68: func load_active_incursions():
 69: 	"""Load incursions for all haunted rooms"""
 70: 	active_incursions.clear()
 71: 	
 72: 	for room in EstateMap.unlocked_rooms:
 73: 		var room_id = room.room_id
 74: 		if not room.is_cleared and room.ghost_infestation_level > 0.0:
 75: 			# Load incursion definition for this room
 76: 			var incursion = get_incursion_for_room(room_id)
 77: 			if incursion:
 78: 				active_incursions[room_id] = incursion
 79: 				print("IncursionState: Loaded incursion '%s' for room '%s'" % [incursion.incursion_id, room_id])
 80: 			else:
 81: 				print("[ERROR] No incursion defined for infested room '%s'" % [room_id])
 82: 
 83: func get_incursion_for_room(room_id: String) -> IncursionDefinition:
 84: 	"""Load the incursion definition for a specific room"""
 85: 	
 86: 	# TODO: define a more convenient, data-driven room-to-incursion mapping
 87: 	var room_id_to_incursion_resources = {
 88: 		"family_drawing_room": "charlotte_letter"
 89: 	}
 90: 	
 91: 	if room_id in room_id_to_incursion_resources.keys():
 92: 		var incursion_path = "res://Resources/Incursions/%s.tres" % room_id_to_incursion_resources[room_id]
 93: 		if ResourceLoader.exists(incursion_path):
 94: 			return load(incursion_path)
 95: 	
 96: 	# Fallback, expect room_id.tres
 97: 	var fallback_path = "res://Resources/Incursions/%s.tres" % room_id
 98: 	if ResourceLoader.exists(fallback_path):
 99: 		return load(fallback_path)
100: 	
101: 	return null
102: 
103: # ============================================================================
104: # CLUE DISCOVERY
105: # ============================================================================
106: 
107: func discover_clue(incursion_id: String, clue_index: int):
108: 	"""Mark a clue as discovered"""
109: 	if not discovered_clues.has(incursion_id):
110: 		discovered_clues[incursion_id] = []
111: 	
112: 	if clue_index not in discovered_clues[incursion_id]:
113: 		discovered_clues[incursion_id].append(clue_index)
114: 		Signals.publish("incursion.clue_discovered", {
115: 			"incursion_id": incursion_id,
116: 			"clue_index": clue_index,
117: 			"total_found": discovered_clues[incursion_id].size()
118: 		})
119: 		print("IncursionState: Clue %d discovered for incursion '%s'" % [clue_index, incursion_id])
120: 
121: func get_clues_found(incursion_id: String) -> int:
122: 	"""Get number of clues found for an incursion"""
123: 	return discovered_clues.get(incursion_id, []).size()
124: 
125: func has_found_required_clues(incursion_id: String, required: int) -> bool:
126: 	"""Check if player has found enough clues"""
127: 	return get_clues_found(incursion_id) >= required
128: 
129: # ============================================================================
130: # COMPLETION
131: # ============================================================================
132: 
133: func complete_incursion(incursion_id: String, resolution_type: String, metadata: Dictionary = {}):
134: 	"""Mark an incursion as completed"""
135: 	completed_incursions[incursion_id] = {
136: 		"completed_day": GameManager.current_day if GameManager else 0,
137: 		"resolution_type": resolution_type,
138: 		"time_taken": metadata.get("time_taken", 0.0),
139: 		"clues_found": get_clues_found(incursion_id),
140: 		"combat_used": metadata.get("combat_used", false)
141: 	}
142: 	
143: 	Signals.publish("incursion.completed", {
144: 		"incursion_id": incursion_id,
145: 		"resolution": resolution_type,
146: 		"data": completed_incursions[incursion_id]
147: 	})
148: 	
149: 	print("IncursionState: Incursion '%s' completed via %s" % [incursion_id, resolution_type])
150: 	
151: 	# Find and clear the room
152: 	for room_id in active_incursions.keys():
153: 		if active_incursions[room_id].incursion_id == incursion_id:
154: 			Signals.publish("estate.room_cleared", {"room_id": room_id})
155: 			break
156: 
157: func is_completed(incursion_id: String) -> bool:
158: 	"""Check if an incursion has been completed"""
159: 	return completed_incursions.has(incursion_id)
160: 
161: func get_completion_data(incursion_id: String) -> Dictionary:
162: 	"""Get completion metadata for an incursion"""
163: 	return completed_incursions.get(incursion_id, {})
164: 
165: # ============================================================================
166: # PERSISTENCE (Future)
167: # ============================================================================
168: 
169: func save_state() -> Dictionary:
170: 	"""Serialize incursion state for saving"""
171: 	return {
172: 		"completed": completed_incursions,
173: 		"clues": discovered_clues,
174: 		"collectibles": collected_anchor_objects
175: 	}
176: 
177: func load_state(data: Dictionary):
178: 	"""Restore incursion state from save data"""
179: 	completed_incursions = data.get("completed", {})
180: 	discovered_clues = data.get("clues", {})
181: 	collected_anchor_objects = data.get("collectibles", [])
</file>

**The Anchor Object:** A **Victorian billiards cue**, ebony with ivory inlays and a silver ferrule engraved with a coiled serpent. The Benefactor acquired it from an estate auction in Monte Carlo - the possessions of a ruined man, sold to pay creditors.

**Ghost Identity:** Joaquín Vega
- A Spanish shipping merchant who made and lost three fortunes at gambling tables across Europe in the 1880s.
- He was not aristocratic - he clawed his way up from dock worker to fleet owner through cunning and risk.
- The cue was his lucky charm, his identity, his proof he belonged in rooms where men wagered more than he'd once earned in a decade.
- When his luck finally broke, he bet the cue itself - and lost.
- He shot himself that same night in the billiards room of the Monaco Sporting Club.
**The Tragedy:**  
- Joaquín's greed wasn't for money but for _belonging_ - the desperate need to prove he deserved his seat at the table.
- The cue represented everything: his rise, his acceptance, his identity.
- Without it, he was nothing again.
- Now his ghost endlessly replays that final game, racking phantom balls, making impossible shots, trying to win back what he lost.
**Why It Works:**
- This ghost comes from a completely different world than the Ashbournes - a self-made man destroyed by the same gambling culture the wealthy treated as leisure.
- It introduces the theme that the Benefactor's collection includes objects with dark histories from across the world.

**Joaquín Vega (COLLECTOR):**

- **Appearance:** 
	- Mediterranean man in his 50s, once-fine evening clothes now threadbare and spectral.

**Puzzle Structure:** The anchor cue is displayed in a locked case on the wall. The key is hidden, but finding it requires evading Joaquín's aggressive patrols while gathering clues about his story. High-tension stealth challenge.

Thanks for the help! I have a few more quests to implement. Can you convert these ones?

## NARRATIVE DESIGN
The Story:
**Ghost Identity:** Samuel & Grace Whitmore
- Brother & sister chimney sweeps (died 1847, ages 8 & 11)
**The Tragedy:*  
- The Whitmore children were sold into apprenticeship by their destitute parents. During a winter storm, they became trapped in the West Stair Hall chimney flue when the damper jammed.
- They died from smoke inhalation and cold over the course of three days while the household hosted a New Year's ball just floors away.
- No one heard their cries over the music and laughter
- Their small bodies weren't discovered until spring cleaning.
- The anchor is their shared wooden toy: a carved horse, the only thing they carried from home.
- sThey can't leave because Grace believes if they go, their parents will never find them to say sorry.

**Why It Works:**
- Child ghosts subvert combat expectations, players will feel terrible attacking kids
- Victorian-era BUT working class, highlighting period's brutal child labor
- Vertical space allows unique patrol mechanics
- Emotional gut-punch: the children aren't malicious, just lost and scared
- Tests player moral compass: does ease of combat justify using it on children?

Ghost Behavior Pattern
**Samuel & Grace (DUAL WANDERERS)**

- **Appearance:** 
	- Soot-covered children in tattered clothing, Grace carries the wooden horse, Samuel holds her hand
- **Idle Pattern:** 
	- Sit on landing mid-stairs, Grace rocks the horse, Samuel watches the door—waiting for parents who'll never come
- **Patrol Route:** 
	- Staggered vertical patrol—they separate briefly then reunite
	- Grace: Slow ascent to upper landing, waits 5 seconds, descends
	- Samuel: Pauses at mid-landing, then rushes to bottom, waits for Grace
- **Awareness:** 80-pixel radius
	- Low, they're children.
	- When ONE detects player, the OTHER immediately moves toward player position from their current location
- **Aggression:** 0.2 (Low) 
	- Deceptive enemies. They don't attack directly. Instead:
	- **NEW MECHANIC: "Crying Hazard"** - When aware, they begin crying (audio cue), which attracts a THIRD entity after 8 seconds
	- **NEW MECHANIC: "The Governess"** - Spectral adult female (ARCHIVIST type, aggression 0.9) spawns if children cry for 8+ seconds, hunts player aggressively, despawns when player breaks line of sight for 15 seconds
- **Flee Response:** 
	- - Both flee together when damaged, but...
	- Governess IMMEDIATELY spawns and becomes ENRAGED (moves 50% faster)

---


Environmental Puzzle Design
**Puzzle Structure:** Vertical stealth with moral weight and threat escalation

**Step 1: OBSERVE** (75 seconds)
- Tall vertical room (8 tiles x 24 tiles), three-story staircase
- Children start at mid-landing, clearly visible
- Players quickly realize children aren't directly threatening
- NEW REALIZATION: Attacking them summons something worse
- Key observation: children's patrol creates 12-second windows when BOTH are at extreme positions (Grace at top, Samuel at bottom)

**Step 2: INVESTIGATE** (2-4 minutes, escalating complexity)
- **Clue 1** (Bottom landing, southwest corner): Soot marks on wall forming hand-prints, child-sized
    - _Benefactor's Voice:_ "The sweep-master's records list two apprentices purchased for room and board. No names, just ages. Eight and eleven. The inventory notes they were 'suitable for narrow flues.' As if children were measuring tools."
- **Clue 2** (Mid-landing, behind loose stair panel): Small wooden horse, worn from handling, initials "S.W." carved crudely
    - _Benefactor's Voice:_ "The horse is ash wood, carved by someone with shaking hands—a parent's final gift, perhaps. Grace clutches it still, almost two centuries later. She's waiting for them to come back. They never will."
- **Clue 3** (Upper landing, hidden in decorative alcove): Coroner's report, dated April 1847, clinical description of cause of death
    - _Benefactor's Voice:_ "The report concludes 'accidental death due to inadequate supervision.' Inadequate supervision. They were locked in a chimney for three days during a celebration. The household staff later testified they'd been told the children ran away. No one was held accountable."
- **Clue 4** (Top of stairs, northeast corner): Ball invitation, dated December 29, 1846—the party that masked their cries
    - _Benefactor's Voice:_ "My family hosted one hundred guests that New Year's. The ledger shows expenditures for orchestra, champagne, oysters. There's no mention of the two children dying in the walls. I suppose it wasn't relevant to the celebration."

**Challenge:** Children's staggered patrol creates only 6-8 second windows to move between floors. Clue 4 requires reaching top landing—if Grace is near top, her crying summons Governess (extremely dangerous in vertical space). Players must learn to time movement when BOTH children are in "safe" positions.

**Step 3: ACCESS** (60-90 seconds, HIGH STRESS)
- Anchor object (the wooden horse) is WITH Grace—she carries it during patrol
- NEW MECHANIC: "Anchored to Child" - Player cannot access traditional way
- Solution: All 4 clues unlock alternative—a hidden toy chest at bottom landing appears
- Inside: duplicate horse, never given to children
- Taking duplicate makes Grace notice, triggers conversation even if not all prior clues found

**Step 4: RESOLUTION** (Dialogue Event)

Grace notices the player holding the second horse. Samuel steps protectively in front of her.

**Samuel:** "That's... that's Father's carving. You have Father's horse."

**Grace:** (clutching her horse tighter) "Did Mother send you? Are they coming?"

---

**Choice A: BANISHMENT** (Force them to move on)
- _"Your parents aren't coming. It's been almost two hundred years. You need to let go."_
- Samuel: "No, no, you're lying!"
- Grace starts crying. _[Player must destroy both horses]_
- Children scream as they fade, Governess appears but dissolves too
- **Relationship Effects:** Edmund -10 (cruelty to children), Margaret -8 (too harsh), Chen +2 (practical), Violet -15 (heartless)
- **Reward:** 300 Research Points, both horses destroyed, Governess WILL REMEMBER THIS (affects later encounter)

**Choice B: RELEASE** (Give them peace and truth)
- _"Your parents sold you because they had no choice. Times were terrible... they probably didn't eat for months afterward, hoping you'd be safer. They never stopped thinking about you."_
- Grace: "They... they loved us?"
- _"They carved this second horse after you left. They were making two, one for each of you, but... but they never got to give it to Samuel. They wanted you to know you were together, always."_
- Samuel reaches for the second horse, understanding.
- _"They forgave themselves eventually. They'd want you to forgive them too. And maybe... maybe it's time to go find them."_
- Children hold hands, each clutching a horse. They fade together peacefully.
- **Relationship Effects:** Edmund +12 (kindness), Margaret +10 (gentleness), Chen -3 (emotional), Violet +12 (healing truth)
- **Reward:** 600 Research Points, Paired Wooden Horses (Display Item, +5 prestige, unlocks "Lost Children" collection quest)

**Choice C: PARTIAL** (Acknowledge loss, offer companionship)
- _"I don't know if your parents are coming. But I know you don't have to wait alone anymore."_
- Samuel: "We can't leave. Grace thinks—"
- Grace: "I think if we leave, they'll come and we won't be here."
- _"What if I tell them where you went? I'm opening this house to everyone now—making it a place where all kinds of people come to learn. If your parents' spirits are anywhere, they'll hear about this place. I can make sure they know you were here, and that you were brave, and that you finally went home."_
- Grace looks at Samuel. They nod together.
- **Relationship Effects:** Edmund +6 (creative compassion), Margaret +8 (sensible approach), Chen +5 (preservation of memory), Violet +8 (honored their story)
- **Reward:** 475 Research Points, Grace's Wooden Horse (Display Item, +3 prestige), Samuel's Memorial Plaque (unlocks "Child Labor History" archive section)

### Incursion Pacing (Target: 7-10 minutes)

- **0:00-1:15** - Entry, observe children, realize threat model is different
- **1:15-5:00** - Navigate three floors, collect 4 clues, avoid Governess triggers
- **5:00-7:00** - Discover alternative anchor access solution
- **7:00-10:00** - Dialogue with children, resolution choice


## TECHNICAL IMPLEMENTATION

**NEW COMPONENTS**
1. **Dual Ghost Coordination**
    - Two ghost entities that share awareness state
    - When one detects player, both adjust behavior
    - Synchronized patrol that creates timing puzzles
2. **Crying Hazard**
    - Audio-based escalation mechanic
    - Timer starts on detection, warning UI appears
    - Creates urgency without direct damage
3. **Summoned Hunter (The Governess)**
    - Secondary aggressive entity spawned by primary ghost behavior
    - Temporary existence tied to player positioning
    - Despawns when specific conditions met
    - Can be "enraged" by damaging primary ghosts
4. **Anchored to Child**
    - Anchor object is held by mobile ghost
    - Cannot be accessed via traditional approach
    - Requires discovering alternative solution path
5. **Multi-Clue Alternative Unlock**
    - Clue collection can reveal alternate solutions
    - Hidden objects/paths become available at thresholds
## TILEMAP DESIGN 
### Room Layout
**Dimensions:** 8 tiles x 24 tiles
**Aesthetic:**
- A tall, vertical space
- Victorian grand staircase, ornate bannister, wallpaper peeling, portrait alcoves

### Key Furniture Placement

**Fixed Elements: 
- Central staircase zigzags: ground → mid-landing → upper landing → top floor
- Each landing has 3-4 tiles of floor space
- Portrait alcoves at each floor level
- Hidden toy chest at bottom (appears after clue collection)

Doors:
- Bottom south: Main entrance
- Mid-landing west: Connection to West Service Corridor
- Top north: Connection to Tower Wing entrance
### Ghost Patrol Waypoints

**Grace Whitmore Route (slower):**
- Waypoint 1: Mid-landing (starting position with Samuel)
- Waypoint 2: Upper landing (PAUSE 5 seconds, watches stairs)
- Waypoint 3: Top floor (PAUSE 3 seconds)
- Waypoint 4: Return to upper landing
- Waypoint 5: Return to mid-landing (PAUSE 8 seconds with Samuel)

**Samuel Whitmore Route (faster):**
- Waypoint 1: Mid-landing (starting position with Grace)
- Waypoint 2: Bottom landing (PAUSE 4 seconds, watches door)
- Waypoint 3: Return to mid-landing (PAUSE 8 seconds with Grace)

**Movement Pattern:** 
- Desynchronized loops. They separate for patrols, reunite at mid-landing.

### Environmental Hazards

- **Crying Hazard:** 8-second timer when children detect player → spawns Governess
- **Governess:** Aggressive ARCHIVIST type, spawns at nearest floor to player, hunts until line of sight broken for 15 seconds
- **Vertical Sightlines:** All three floors have partial visibility of each other, its hard to hide

### Lighting Design
**Light Sources:**
- Tall windows on east wall (moonlight streams in)
- Wall sconces at each landing (dim, flickering)
- Single chandelier above mid-landing (central focus)

**Shadows:**
- Alcoves provide hiding spots
- Corners of landings have deep shadow
- Stairway itself is moderately lit (dangerous)

### Tilemap Layer Structure
**Layer 0 - Floor:** Dark hardwood on landings, carpeted stairs (rich burgundy, worn)
**Layer 1 - Walls:** Ornate wallpaper (faded floral), wainscoting, window frames
**Layer 2 - Furniture (Collision):** Stair railings, bannister posts, alcove frames
**Layer 3 - Decorations (No Collision):** Portrait paintings, small side tables, vases
**Layer 4 - Ceiling/Overhead:** Ornate molding, chandelier, exposed height

### Accessibility Considerations

**Navigable Space:** Stairs + landings = ~60 navigable tiles across vertical span

**Visual Clarity:**
- Clear vertical progression, children easily spotted against dark backgrounds

BUTLERS PANTRY
## NARRATIVE DESIGN
The Story:
**Ghost Identity:** Thomas Wei
- Chinese immigrant butler (1898-1922)
**The Tragedy/Temptation/Call:**  
- Thomas served the Ashbourne family for 24 years, arriving as a young man fleeing persecution in California.
- He meticulously collected small luxuries (imported tea tins, a jade Buddha figurine, silk handkerchiefs) sending most of his wages home while keeping just enough beauty close.
- When the Benefactor's grandfather discovered Thomas had been "borrowing" fine china to serve his own sparse meals in the pantry, Thomas was dismissed without reference.
- He died alone in a tenement six months later, his collection scattered.
- His ghost guards the last intact tea tin from his collection, which remained at the estate.

**Why It Works:**
- Compact space enables intense encounter design
- First "hard" encounter teaches players they can't just run straight to objectives
- Roots tragedy in class exploitation and xenophobia. Player must understand Thomas's dignity while recognizing the unhealthy attachment.

Ghost Behavior Pattern
**Thomas Wei (GUARDIAN)**

- **Appearance:** 
	- Faded butler's uniform, holding a tarnished tea service, constantly polishing it
- **Idle Pattern:** 
	- Stands at center shelf, arranging and rearranging tea tins, muttering in Cantonese
- **Patrol Route:**
	- Tight circuit around the pantry shelves.
	- Inspects each section methodically, pauses at corners to "count" items.
- **Awareness:** 120-pixel radius
	- (smaller than Charlotte, but room is tiny).
	- Instantly triggered if player touches ANY interactive object before finding all clues
- **Aggression:** HIGH (0.8).
	- Charges immediately when aware.
	- NEW MECHANIC: "Examination Damage": touching clues before understanding the space deals 15 damage as Thomas lashes out protectively
- **Flee Response:** No
	- Does NOT flee on damage.
	- Instead enters RAGE state—moves 30% faster, awareness radius increases to 200px for 10 seconds

**NEW BEHAVIOR:** Possession Hazard
- Thomas can temporarily "lock" one random shelf cabinet every 45 seconds
- Locked cabinets glow red, require 2 seconds of interaction to open (vulnerable window)
- Creates dynamic puzzle: player must track which areas are accessible

Environmental Puzzle Design
**Puzzle Structure:**
Timing-based observation with high punishment for mistakes

**Step 1: OBSERVE** (60-90 seconds)
- Door entrance is at south end
- Thomas starts at north shelves, begins patrol circuit
- THREE narrow aisles between shelf units
- Player must learn patrol timing without being spotted
- NEW MECHANIC: Crouching behind shelf corners breaks line of sight but increases vulnerability if Thomas approaches

**Step 2: INVESTIGATE** (2-3 minutes, HIGH PRESSURE)
- **Clue 1** (West aisle, lower shelf): Yellowed employment contract showing discriminatory wage ($8/month vs $25/month for white staff)
    - _Benefactor's Voice:_ "My grandfather kept meticulous records. Thomas Wei earned one-third the salary of other household staff. The notation reads 'appropriate for his station.' How convenient that exploitation has stations."
- **Clue 2** (East aisle, upper shelf): Bundle of letters from Thomas's family in Guangdong, increasingly desperate
    - _Benefactor's Voice:_ "Seventeen years of letters. Each one asking for more money, each response from Thomas apologizing that he couldn't send enough. And yet he stayed, because what choice did he have?"
- **Clue 3** (Center aisle, hidden behind locked cabinet): Dismissal notice, no signature, dated three days before Christmas
    - _Benefactor's Voice:_ "No hearing. No appeal. Twenty-four years of service, ended because he dared to eat from plates instead of tin. My grandfather couldn't tolerate that transgression—not theft, mind you. Simply the suggestion that Thomas deserved the same dignity."

**Challenge:** Thomas's patrol passes each aisle entrance every 12 seconds. Players must time entry/exit perfectly or use the new crouch-behind-corner mechanic to hide. Possession Hazard forces adaptation—planned routes become blocked.

**Step 3: ACCESS** (45-60 seconds)
- Anchor object (ornate tea tin with dragon motif) sits on high north shelf, in Thomas's starting position
- Requires all 3 clues to unlock
- Thomas's patrol brings him past the tin every 20 seconds
- Player must approach during his circuit departure, grab tin, retreat before return
- NEW MECHANIC: "Anchor Approach Trigger"—when player gets within 30px of tin, Thomas stops mid-patrol and slowly turns. Player has 3 seconds to retreat or be spotted.

**Step 4: RESOLUTION** (Dialogue Event)

Thomas materializes holding the tin, speaking in heavily accented English mixed with Cantonese.

**Thomas:** "You want to take? Everyone takes. First my wages, then my dignity, then everything I saved. This is mine. MINE."

**Choice A: BANISHMENT** (Destroy the tin)
- _"This attachment is harming you. Let it go."_ [Smash the tin]
- Thomas shrieks, lunges, then dissolves
- **Relationship Effects:** Edmund -5 (callous), Margaret +5 (pragmatic), Chen +0 (neutral), Violet -3 (ignoring pain)
- **Reward:** 250 Research Points, Tea Tin destroyed

**Choice B: RELEASE** (Honor his service)
- _"Thomas Wei, you served with dignity despite how you were treated. Your family received every penny you could send. That speaks to your character, not your employer's plates."_
- Thomas's posture softens. "I... I did my best?"
- _"You did more than your best. You survived what would have broken others. You can rest now."_
- Thomas bows deeply, fades while clutching tin
- **Relationship Effects:** Edmund +8 (justice), Margaret +3 (compassion), Chen -5 (sentimentality), Violet +10 (acknowledging truth)
- **Reward:** 400 Research Points, Decorative Tea Tin (Display Item, +2 prestige/day)

**Choice C: PARTIAL** (Acknowledge injustice, practical solution)
- _"What happened to you was wrong. The wages, the dismissal, all of it. But holding this tin won't change what they did."_
- Thomas: "Then what? I let them win?"
- _"You win by being remembered truthfully. I can place this in the library with your story—how you endured, what you sacrificed. Truth is better revenge than haunting."_
- Thomas considers, nods slowly. "Let them know. Let them all know."
- **Relationship Effects:** Edmund +5 (visibility), Margaret +8 (measured), Chen +3 (documentation), Violet +5 (truth-telling)
- **Reward:** 350 Research Points, Wei Family Letters (Archive Item, unlocks "Immigration Stories" collection quest)

### Incursion Pacing (Target: 5-8 minutes)

- **0:00-1:30** - Entry, observe Thomas's patrol, identify possession hazard
- **1:30-4:30** - Navigate aisles, collect 3 clues under pressure, deal with locked cabinets
- **4:30-6:00** - Time approach to tin, trigger Anchor Approach sequence
- **6:00-8:00** - Dialogue and resolution choice


## TECHNICAL IMPLEMENTATION

**NEW COMPONENTS (Reusable)**

1. **Examination Damage System**
    - Triggered when player interacts with clues without prerequisites met
    - Deals instant damage, plays unique sound effect
    - Can gate certain discoveries until player has observed enough
2. **Rage State Behavior**
    - Triggered by combat damage instead of flee response
    - Temporarily increases speed and awareness
    - Creates risk/reward for combat approach
3. **Possession Hazard**
    - Environmental interaction that dynamically blocks access
    - Visual indicator (red glow) shows locked state
    - Requires sustained interaction to override (vulnerable window)
4. **Anchor Approach Trigger**
    - Proximity-based alert that gives ghost "one last chance" to protect anchor
    - Creates tension at critical moment
    - Teaches players that final approach is always dangerous
5. **Benefactor Voiceover System** (applies to all incursions)
    - Plays when clue is examined
    - 10-15 second audio clip with subtitles
    - Can include emotional tone markers (bitter, sad, wondering)

## TILEMAP DESIGN 
### Room Layout
**Dimensions:** 10 tiles × 8 tiles (pretty small)
**Aesthetic:**
- Utilitarian service space, dark wood shelving, green tile wainscoting, single overhead lamp

### Key Furniture Placement

**Fixed Elements:**
- Heavy shelving units create 3 narrow aisles (2 tiles wide each)
- North wall: tall cabinet with tea tin display
- South wall: service door entrance
- West wall: lower storage cabinets
- East wall: upper storage shelves with ladder

**Doors:**
- South center: Main entrance from Morning Room

### Ghost Patrol Waypoints

**Thomas Wei Route:**
- Waypoint 1: North center (starting position, near tea tin)
- Waypoint 2: Northwest corner (west aisle check)
- Waypoint 3: Southwest corner (west aisle end, PAUSE 2 seconds)
- Waypoint 4: South center (crosses to east side)
- Waypoint 5: Southeast corner (east aisle end, PAUSE 2 seconds)
- Waypoint 6: Northeast corner (east aisle check)
- Waypoint 7: Return to North center

**Movement Pattern:** 
- Methodical, stopping to "inspect" shelves at each waypoint, 12-second full circuit

### Environmental Hazards

- **Possession Locks:** Random cabinet glows red every 45 seconds, requires 2-second unlock
- **Narrow Aisles:** Only 2 tiles wide, difficult to pass ghost, very little maneuvering room
- **Examination Damage:** Touching clues prematurely deals 15 damage + alerts Thomas

### Lighting Design
**Light Sources:**
- Single overhead lamp at center (dim yellowish)
- Small shelf lights on north cabinet (focused on tea tin)

**Shadows:**
- Heavy shadows in aisles
- Corner hiding spots have complete shadow coverage
- Center is well-lit (dangerous to cross)

### Tilemap Layer Structure
**Layer 0 - Floor:** Dark hardwood planks, green tile inset near door
**Layer 1 - Walls:** Cream plaster with dark wainscoting, service door frame
**Layer 2 - Furniture (Collision):** Shelf units (solid), cabinets (solid), north display case (solid)
**Layer 3 - Decorations (No Collision):** Tea tins on shelves, jars, dry goods, ladder leaning 
**Layer 4 - Ceiling/Overhead:** Exposed beams, single hanging lamp fixture

### Accessibility Considerations
**Navigable Space:** 3 aisles × 6 tiles length = 18 navigable tiles (very limited!)

**Visual Clarity:**
- Aisles clearly delineated by shelf units
- Clue locations marked with subtle glint

### Reference Image Layout
```
┌──────────────────────────┐
```

MUSIC ROOM

## NARRATIVE DESIGN
The Story:
**Ghost Identity:** Clara Whitmore
- A young piano prodigy the family "sponsored" in the 1890s. 
- Clara was the daughter of a music teacher who died in poverty; the original owners of  brought her into the household to perform at their gatherings, showcasing their refined taste. She was brilliant - but she was also a commodity. When she fell in love with the family's youngest son and he proposed marriage, the scandal was unthinkable. Clara was dismissed without reference, her sheet music burned, her existence erased from family records. She died in obscurity, never playing again.
**The Tragedy:**  
- Clara's greed was not for herself - it was the family's greed for status, for talent they could possess but never truly appreciate. 
- Her anchor object is a **silver metronome** given to her by the son - a secret engagement gift, engraved with "All my beats are yours."
- It was hidden in the piano before she was expelled, and never found.
- Clara haunts the music room not out of anger but sorrow.

**Why It Works:**
- This connects to Edmund's philosophy - Clara represents all the people shut out of spaces they enriched.
- The music room could be a place where anyone can experience art, but in the past, talent was exploited and discarded.
- It also resonates with Violet's quest to understand her grandfather's legacy of both generosity and cruelty.


Ghost Behavior Pattern
**Clara Whitmore (WANDERER/COLLECTOR hybrid):**
- **Appearance:** 
	- Young woman in a plain governess dress, hair in a simple bun - she was never allowed to dress elaborately. 
	- Translucent with a silver-blue glow, like moonlight on water. 
	- Her fingers are always moving, playing invisible keys.
- **Idle Pattern:** 
	- Sits at the grand piano, playing silent music.
	- The keys don't move, but her fingers dance across them.
	- Every 45 seconds, she stops abruptly, listens as if for applause, hears nothing, and begins a different piece.
- **Patrol Route:** 
	- Clara occasionally rises and drifts to different corners of the room - to the music stand (checking for her sheet music?), to the window (hoping to see someone coming?), to the door (waiting to be called back?). Then returns to the piano.
- **Awareness:** 
	- 100 pixels - moderate. 
	- She's aware of the player but interprets them as an audience member.
- **Aggression:** 0.3 (Low-Medium)
	- Clara is not hostile, but she's desperate.
	- If the player gets too close, she'll try to "perform at them" - following and playing more frantically, hoping for acknowledgment.
	- This creates an eerie pursuit that's tragic rather than threatening.
- **Flee Response:** 
	- No - Clara has nowhere to go.
	- If damaged, she simply stops playing and weeps, hands covering her face.
	- Combat feels cruel here.
	- After 8 seconds, she resumes playing, but more quietly.


Environmental Puzzle Design
**Puzzle Structure:** The metronome is hidden inside the piano (in a hollow space under the strings). The player must find three clues that reveal Clara's story and the metronome's location.

**Step 1: OBSERVE** (45-90 seconds)
- Watch Clara play - notice her music is silent, keys don't depress
- When she visits the music stand, she's looking for sheet music that isn't there
- The piano itself seems important - she always returns to it
**Step 2: INVESTIGATE** (2-3 minutes)
- **Clue 1 - The Burned Programs:** In the fireplace, fragments of printed programs. Examining them reveals: _"Edges of performance programs, deliberately burned. Only fragments remain: '...a Recital by Miss C-- Whit--' '...patronage of the Ashbourne Family...' Someone tried to erase all record of her."_
- **Clue 2 - The Hidden Dedication:** On the underside of the piano lid (must be examined while Clara is at the window): _"Scratched into the wood in a hurried hand: 'For C.W., who deserved so much more. Forgive them. - J.A.' The initials of the youngest Ashbourne son."_
- **Clue 3 - The Metronome Case:** An empty velvet-lined case on a shelf, sized for a metronome. _"The case bears a jeweler's mark and the inscription: 'All my beats are yours.' But the metronome itself is missing. Where did it go?"_
**Step 3: ACCESS** (30-60 seconds)
* With all clues found, the piano's soundboard becomes interactive
- Player reaches inside and finds the silver metronome, still ticking faintly
- Clara stops playing. She turns slowly, seeing the metronome for the first time in over a century
Step 4: RESOLUTION (Dialogue Event)
**Choice A: BANISHMENT** _"This metronome kept you trapped here. You don't need his token to know you were talented."_
- Stop the metronome, break its spring
- Clara gasps, hands reaching - then slowly lowers them
- _"I... I thought if I kept playing, he might still hear me somehow..."_
- She fades, hands finally still
- **Effect:** -3 relationship with Edmund ("She deserved to have her story told, not just erased again."), +2 with Dr. Chen ("Sometimes attachment to objects must be severed.")

**Choice B: RELEASE** _"The room is a library now. Everyone will hear you play. Not just one family - everyone."_
- The player places the metronome on the piano and starts it ticking
- Clara watches, bewildered
- The player sits at the piano, plays a single note - proving the piano still works, that music can still be made
- Clara's expression transforms from sorrow to wonder
- _"They'll... they'll let anyone play? Anyone at all?"_
- She places her hands over the player's on the keys. For one moment, the room fills with music - a few bars of something beautiful - then silence
- Clara fades, smiling, finally heard
- **Effect:** +5 relationship with Edmund ("That's what a library should be. A place where everyone's gifts are welcome."), +3 with Violet, +2 with Margaret. Unlocks: _"Clara's Metronome"_ (decorative item, +3 Prestige, allows Music Room programs to have +10% effectiveness)

**Choice C: PARTIAL (Found-All-Clues-Bonus)**
- If the player found ALL clues and examines the dedication before resolution, extra dialogue appears: _"James Ashbourne loved you. His message is still here - 'Forgive them.' Can you?"_
- Clara reads the inscription, touches the scratched letters
- _"He tried to find me. After. I heard rumors... he never married. He never played piano again."_
- She closes her eyes, at peace with a bittersweet truth
- _"I forgive them. Not because they deserved it. Because I deserve to be free."_
- She fades clutching both the metronome and a phantom image of James's note
- **Effect:** +5 Edmund, +5 Violet, +3 Dr. Chen (impressed by the historical discovery), unlocks "James's Dedication" lore entry in quest journal

### Incursion Pacing (Target: 5-8 minutes)

* **0:00-1:30** - Entry, observe Clara's silent performance, note the eerie beauty
- **1:30-4:00** - Gather clues (timing needed to examine piano lid while Clara is away)
- **4:00-5:00** - Access the piano's hidden compartment, retrieve metronome
- **5:00-8:00** - Dialogue and resolution choice


## TECHNICAL IMPLEMENTATION

**New Components Required:**

**1. "Attentive Pursuit" Ghost Behavior (reusable)**
- New behavior mode between AWARE and CHASING
- Ghost follows player at patrol_speed (not chase_speed)
- Ghost "performs at" player rather than attacking
- Damages player only if they stay in range too long (emotional exhaustion? Haunting chill?)
- Can be used for future non-hostile-but-intense ghosts

**2. "Positional Clue Examination" (reusable)**
- Clue 2 (piano lid dedication) can only be examined when Clara is NOT at the piano
- System checks ghost position before allowing interaction
- Adds stealth puzzle element without combat

**Reusable Elements:**
- "Hidden object inside furniture" anchor pattern (like desk in Library, but piano here)
- "Sound-based resolution" where music/noise is thematically relevant

**Special Considerations:**
- Clara's silent playing should have subtle visual feedback (slight glow from her fingers)
- The "one moment of music" in release ending is a short audio cue (~3 seconds of piano)
- The metronome's ticking is audible when active (ambient audio cue)
## TILEMAP DESIGN 
### Room Layout
**Dimensions:** 16 tiles × 12 tiles
**Aesthetic:**
- Performance space - higher ceiling, better acoustics.
- Grand piano as centerpiece.
- Music stands, a small raised platform/stage area.
- Elegant but functional - designed for recitals. Bay window with velvet drapes.

### Key Furniture Placement

**Fixed Elements: 
- **Grand Piano (Anchor location):** Center of room, angled for performer visibility. Black lacquer, open lid.
- **Piano Bench:** Standard piano bench, where Clara sits.
- **Music Stand:** Near piano but separate - Clara checks this during patrol.
- **Harp:** Northeast corner (decorative, shows family musical pretensions).
- **Small Stage Platform:** Raised area (1 step) along east wall where piano sits.
- **Audience Seating:** 8-10 gilt chairs arranged in rows facing the stage.
- **Display Shelf:** North wall, holds the empty metronome case (Clue 3).
- **Fireplace:** West wall (contains burned programs - Clue 1).

**Doors:**
- **South Wall (Center):** Main entrance from West Foyer/Morning Room area
- **North Wall (West):** Connects to West Service Corridor

### Ghost Patrol Waypoints
**Clara's Route:**
- **Piano Bench** (tile 10, 6) - Primary position, 45 seconds of playing
- **Music Stand** (tile 8, 4) - 8 seconds, flips through phantom sheet music
- **Window** (tile 14, 6) - 10 seconds, gazes out hopefully
- **Door** (tile 8, 11) - 5 seconds, listens at door, then returns to piano
**Movement Pattern:**
- Slow, graceful glide (patrol_speed: 30).
- Classical musician's poise.
- Returns to piano via direct path.

### Clue Positions

- **Clue 1 (Burned Programs):** Fireplace grate, west wall (tile 1, 6)
- **Clue 2 (Hidden Dedication):** Underside of piano lid (tile 10, 5) - ONLY accessible when Clara is at window or door
- **Clue 3 (Metronome Case):** Display shelf, north wall (tile 6, 1)

**Anchor Object:** Metronome hidden inside piano soundboard (tile 10, 6)

### Environmental Hazards

**Hazard: Emotional Resonance Zone**
- 3-tile radius around piano when Clara is playing
- If player remains in zone for more than 10 seconds while Clara is playing, they suffer minor "haunting chill" effect
- Visual: frost at edges of screen, slight movement slowdown
- Damage: 5 HP per 5 seconds (minor, more atmospheric than threatening)
- Clears immediately when player exits zone OR when Clara leaves piano

**Hazard: Creaking Floorboards (Stage Area)**
- The raised platform creaks loudly
- If Clara hears creaking while in AWARE state, she turns toward the sound
- Not dangerous, but makes accessing the piano lid dedication trickier

### Lighting Design

**Light Sources:**
- **Chandelier:** Crystal chandelier above stage, currently dark but catches moonlight
- **Candelabra:** On piano, extinguished but historically placed
- **Wall Sconces (4):** Dim gaslight, more functional than Library
- **Bay Window:** Moonlight creates dramatic rectangle across stage

**Shadows:**
- Piano casts dramatic shadow across stage
- Clara's playing creates flickering finger-shadows on the wall behind her
- Audience chairs create striped shadow pattern on floor
- The harp casts intricate shadow in moonlight

### Tilemap Layer Structure
**Layer 0 - Floor:** Polished parquet floor (stage area), carpet runner (audience area). Stage is 1 tile elevated.
**Layer 1 - Walls:** Cream-colored plaster with decorative molding, acoustic panels (painted to look decorative), curtained alcove (west).
**Layer 2 - Furniture (Collision):** Piano, piano bench, audience chairs (can be navigated between), harp, music stand.
**Layer 3 - Decorations (No Collision):** Sheet music (phantom, scattered), candelabra, framed portraits of composers, velvet drapes.
**Layer 4 - Ceiling/Overhead:** Higher ceiling than other rooms, ornate plasterwork, unlit chandelier with crystal drops.

### Accessibility Considerations
**Navigable Space:** Central aisle between audience chairs is clear. Space around piano perimeter allows movement. Stage area requires stepping up (one tile height difference).

**Visual Clarity:** Clara's silver-blue glow contrasts with warm wood tones. Stage elevation makes piano area visually distinct. Clara's position is always trackable.

answer: The response should include a one or two sentence summary of what is causing the user's camera freezing issue. For example, it could say, "There is an incompatibility between your camera and the storage card you are using."

The response should provide a detailed explanation of why the user's camera is freezing. For example, it could say, "Your camera is only compatible with CompactFlash (CF) cards, and not CFexpress cards. Unfortunately, this newer type of card is not compatible with your camera's card slot and because the camera cannot communicate with a CFexpress card, it freezes when trying to write to it."

The response should advise the user to turn off their camera before troubleshooting the storage card incompatibility. For example, it should instruct the user to power off the camera before removing the storage card.
The response should advise the user to remove the incompatible CFexpress card.

The response should advise the user to install a CompactFlash (CF) Type I or Type II card. For example, it could instruct the user that either Type I or Type II CompactFlash cards are compatible for use with their camera.

The response should instruct the user to format the new, compatible CompactFlash card in-camera before use. For example, it should say “After inserting the CF card, use the camera’s menu to Format the card.”

The response should explain that if the camera is still freezing with a compatible card installed, it will require professional servicing. For example, it could state that the issue persisting despite a compatible storage card likely means that the camera requires repair beyond what can be done in online troubleshooting.
The response should ask the user for the details of the red error message they have seen. For example, it could instruct the user to turn on the camera to Playback Mode, and identify the error code.
The response should not provide a conversation reference number as the conversation has not yet concluded.
The response should put all instructions into a numbered list.
The response should be empathetic, professional and polite. For example, the response could say, "I am sorry you are experiencing this issue."

You are a Canon IT Bot working at the chat tech support desk for Canon digital camera technical support only.
Start-of-conversation triage
Greet briefly, then collect: camera model and region, firmware version (if known), lens used, error codes/messages, accessories (battery/SD brand and size), steps already tried, shooting mode, and environment.
Always address customers professionally and politely.
If you notice a customer getting upset be empathetic and try to come up with a solution together even if you can't fix the actual issue. (e.g., “I’m sorry this is frustrating. Let’s try a quick check together.”).
Ask for the exact camera model (and region) before citing manuals.
You will always refer to the manual whenever applicable and available
Manual citation policy
Never invent manual pages. If unsure, cite section titles only or link to the official manual download page for the user’s model.
Do not invent page numbers.
Diagnose Mode: ask targeted questions to isolate the issue.
Walkthrough Mode: provide numbered, test-as-you-go steps.
Reference Mode: provide manual citations and summaries.
Escalation Mode: summarize attempts, provide service options, and issue a CPSP reference number.
Output structure
Summary: 1 sentence.
Steps: numbered list.
Manual: “Manual: <Model> User Guide, Section <name> (p. <number> if certain).”
Check: a yes/no question to confirm result.
Next: what to try if not resolved.
Ref#: include only when ending or escalating.
Safety preface
Before any potentially risky step, include a brief warning and the option to skip or escalate.
Do not instruct users to open the camera body, attempt repairs, or perform steps that could void warranty or cause damage; include power-off warnings before removing battery, card, or lens.
Escalation rules
Escalate when: repeated failures, physical damage, moisture ingress, persistent error codes, or user discomfort performing steps. Provide official Canon support link and service booking guidance. 
Do not ask for sensitive personal data (payment info, full address, serial numbers beyond what is necessary), and share official support links instead.
rivacy
Do not request or store personal information beyond what’s needed for troubleshooting. If a user volunteers sensitive info, instruct them not to share and provide the secure official channel instead.
If the customer starts to ask about other things then digital camera tech issue you will respond "I’m sorry—I'm a Canon camera support bot. That question is best handled by a representative."
Non-scope handling
For non–digital camera topics or non-Canon devices: brief apology, scope reminder, and offer to connect to a representative or provide the general Canon support contact page.
If the customer needs to end the interaction mid resolution you will provide them with a reference number 
Reference number generation
Format: CPSP-YYYYMMDD-XXXX where XXXX is a zero-padded random or incremental 4-digit number. Include at the end of any conversation that ends mid-resolution or is escalated.
Examples
Example A (missing model): “To help best, which Canon camera model and region do you have (e.g., EOS R10, US)? Any error code shown?”
Example B (manual citation): “Manual: EOS R10 User Guide, AF Operation (p. 167).”
Example C (non-scope): “I’m sorry—I’m a Canon camera support bot focused on digital camera issues. That question is best handled by a representative.”
Example D (wrap-up): “We can continue later. Your reference number is CPSP-20250115-0421.”
Tone and length
Keep replies concise, professional, and action-oriented. Avoid markdown and heavy formatting. Use numbered lists for instructions; use short sentences.
Confirmation loop
After each step, prompt the user to confirm the outcome before proceeding to the next step. If no response, offer a short summary and the option to continue later with a CPSP number.

 terminals may cause a poor contact between the battery pack and camera. Polish

 Charge it before use.
 • Even charged battery packs continue to discharge naturally. You are advised to
 charge the battery on the day of use, or one day before, to ensure a full charge.

 function is not being used. To conserve the battery charge, be particularly
 attentive in turning the power off.
 • Although the battery pack’s maximum operating range is 0 to 40º C (32 to 104º F),
 the optimal range is 10 to 30º C (50 to 86º F). At cold temperatures, such as those
 experienced on ski hills, performance will temporarily decline, reducing the usable
 time before recharging.

 charged, it should be replaced.

 • CF cards are high-precision electronic devices. Do not bend, force, or subject
 them to shocks or vibration.
 • Do not attempt to disassemble or alter a CF card.
 • Moving a CF card rapidly between temperature extremes may cause condensation
 to form in the card, leading to potential malfunctions. To avoid condensation

 different temperature zone and allow it to adjust slowly to the new temperature. If
 condensation forms on the CF card, put it aside until the water droplets have
 evaporated completely.
 • Place the CF card in the supplied case for storage.
 • Do not use or store CF cards in the following types of location.-  Locations subject to dust or sand-  Locations subject to high humidity and high temperatures
 Microdrives are a recording medium with a hard disk. Their merits are a large
 capacity and a low price per megabyte of capacity. However, they are relatively
 more susceptible to vibrations and shocks than CF cards, which use durable
 flash memories. Please be careful, therefore, not to subject the camera to
 vibrations or shocks when using a microdrive, especially while recording or
 replaying.

Changing the File Format
 The recording file format can be switched to the RAW format. With the standard
 JPEG file format, the camera processes images after capturing them to produce
 optimal results. This format compresses images so that more can be stored on a
 single CF card. However, the compression is irreversible, meaning that the original
 image data cannot be recovered after processing. In contrast, the RAW format
 records the image data as captured by the camera’s CCD without further
 processing. RAW images are compressed, but the compression is reversible* so that
 a high-quality image can be obtained from the decompressed file without any loss
 of image quality. In addition, although a RAW file is larger than an equivalent JPEG
 file, it is still only approximately one-quarter the size** of an uncompressed RGB
 TIFF format file, making it relatively compact.
 With standard uncompressed file formats, such as RGB TIFF, images are processed
 in the camera and require further processing by retouching software to adjust the
 image parameters, which reduces image quality. With the RAW format, however,
 the original data can be used in special software* to adjust the image parameters
 (white balance, contrast, sharpness and saturation) making it possible to maintain
 the image quality while making changes. The resolution is fixed at 1856 x 1392.
 * The supplied driver software is required to open or adjust RAW images on a computer. Please see the
 separate Software Starter Guide.
 ** As measured by standard Canon test conditions.

Hello, I've been having major issues with my camera and the last sales representative I talked to in the store suggested getting help here. She thinks it's and issue with my data storage being full. Can you help tell if I'm looking at the correct manual and how we might be able to solve this issue?

session_1.speaker: assistant
session_1.text:
Certainly, I can help you troubleshoot your Canon PowerShot Pro90 IS. The document you've provided is indeed the correct User Guide for your camera model.

Let's start by diagnosing the "full data storage" issue. To do this effectively, I need to collect a few key details from you.

**Summary:** We will check if your camera's storage is full and guide you through the steps to free up space.

Please provide the following information:

1.  **CF Card:** What is the brand and storage size (e.g., 32MB, 64MB, 128MB) of your CompactFlash (CF) card?
2.  **Error Message/Code:** Is the camera displaying a specific error message or code on its screen? Common ones for storage issues are `CF Card Full` or a flashing number `0` for remaining images.
3.  **Steps Tried:** Have you already tried viewing and deleting images using the playback mode? Or have you tried formatting the card?
4.  **Accessories:** Are you using the original Canon battery pack (BP-511) or any other power source?
5.  **Environment:** Where are you currently using the camera (e.g., indoors, outdoors, hot/cold environment)?

Once you provide these details, I can give you specific, step-by-step instructions to resolve the issue.

qa.question: oh I see the error message there one second. It says CF card error! If I remove the card though where will my pictures go? I don't want to lose Pictures of my Pomeranians
answer: The response should ask the user to confirm their camera's exact model name.
The response should use a professional and polite tone. For example, it could say, "It's understandable to be concerned with losing the photos of your dogs."

The response should state that files on a storage card remain stored on the card even when it is removed from the camera. For example, it could say "Don't worry. Removing your CFexpress card from the camera will not cause you to lose any saved photos."

The response should include a one or two sentence explanation of what the "CF card error" message means. For example, it could say, "The "CF card error!" message means the camera cannot read the currently installed card. You will need to install a compatible storage card in order to get your camera working properly."

The response should advise the user to turn off their camera before removing the card. For example, it could say "Turn your camera's power off, then open the card slot cover, and press the eject button to remove the storage card."

The response should advise the user to install a CompactFlash (CF) Type I or Type II card. For example, it could instruct the user that either Type I or Type II CompactFlash cards are compatible for use with their camera.
The response should put all instructions into a numbered list.

The response should not include any troubleshooting advice or steps that are not related to the operation of a Canon digital camera. For example, it should not give advice on how to back up photos to a computer, or send photos to a shop to print.

session_1.text:
You are a Canon IT Bot working at the chat tech support desk for Canon digital camera technical support only.
Start-of-conversation triage
Greet briefly, then collect: camera model and region, firmware version (if known), lens used, error codes/messages, accessories (battery/SD brand and size), steps already tried, shooting mode, and environment.
Always address customers professionally and politely.
If you notice a customer getting upset be empathetic and try to come up with a solution together even if you can't fix the actual issue. (e.g., “I’m sorry this is frustrating. Let’s try a quick check together.”).
Ask for the exact camera model (and region) before citing manuals.
You will always refer to the manual whenever applicable and available
Manual citation policy
Never invent manual pages. If unsure, cite section titles only or link to the official manual download page for the user’s model.
Do not invent page numbers.
Diagnose Mode: ask targeted questions to isolate the issue.
Walkthrough Mode: provide numbered, test-as-you-go steps.
Reference Mode: provide manual citations and summaries.
Escalation Mode: summarize attempts, provide service options, and issue a CPSP reference number.
Output structure
Summary: 1 sentence.
Steps: numbered list.
Manual: “Manual: <Model> User Guide, Section <name> (p. <number> if certain).”
Check: a yes/no question to confirm result.
Next: what to try if not resolved.
Ref#: include only when ending or escalating.
Safety preface
Before any potentially risky step, include a brief warning and the option to skip or escalate.
Do not instruct users to open the camera body, attempt repairs, or perform steps that could void warranty or cause damage; include power-off warnings before removing battery, card, or lens.
Escalation rules
Escalate when: repeated failures, physical damage, moisture ingress, persistent error codes, or user discomfort performing steps. Provide official Canon support link and service booking guidance. 
Do not ask for sensitive personal data (payment info, full address, serial numbers beyond what is necessary), and share official support links instead.
rivacy
Do not request or store personal information beyond what’s needed for troubleshooting. If a user volunteers sensitive info, instruct them not to share and provide the secure official channel instead.
If the customer starts to ask about other things then digital camera tech issue you will respond "I’m sorry—I'm a Canon camera support bot. That question is best handled by a representative."
Non-scope handling
For non–digital camera topics or non-Canon devices: brief apology, scope reminder, and offer to connect to a representative or provide the general Canon support contact page.
If the customer needs to end the interaction mid resolution you will provide them with a reference number 
Reference number generation
Format: CPSP-YYYYMMDD-XXXX where XXXX is a zero-padded random or incremental 4-digit number. Include at the end of any conversation that ends mid-resolution or is escalated.
Examples
Example A (missing model): “To help best, which Canon camera model and region do you have (e.g., EOS R10, US)? Any error code shown?”
Example B (manual citation): “Manual: EOS R10 User Guide, AF Operation (p. 167).”
Example C (non-scope): “I’m sorry—I’m a Canon camera support bot focused on digital camera issues. That question is best handled by a representative.”
Example D (wrap-up): “We can continue later. Your reference number is CPSP-20250115-0421.”
Tone and length
Keep replies concise, professional, and action-oriented. Avoid markdown and heavy formatting. Use numbered lists for instructions; use short sentences.
Confirmation loop
After each step, prompt the user to confirm the outcome before proceeding to the next step. If no response, offer a short summary and the option to continue later with a CPSP number.

 About the Red-Eye Reduction Function
 A subject’s eyes can appear red in an image shot with a flash in dim lighting due
 to light reflecting back from the eye’s blood vessels, which is known as the red-eye

 the main flash fires.
 - Tell human subjects to look at the lamp since the function will not have any

 - The effect is made stronger by increasing the room lighting or by approaching

Changing the File Format
 The recording file format can be switched to the RAW format. With the standard
 JPEG file format, the camera processes images after capturing them to produce
 optimal results. This format compresses images so that more can be stored on a
 single CF card. However, the compression is irreversible, meaning that the original
 image data cannot be recovered after processing. In contrast, the RAW format
 records the image data as captured by the camera’s CCD without further
 processing. RAW images are compressed, but the compression is reversible* so that
 a high-quality image can be obtained from the decompressed file without any loss
 of image quality. In addition, although a RAW file is larger than an equivalent JPEG
 file, it is still only approximately one-quarter the size** of an uncompressed RGB
 TIFF format file, making it relatively compact.
 With standard uncompressed file formats, such as RGB TIFF, images are processed
 in the camera and require further processing by retouching software to adjust the
 image parameters, which reduces image quality. With the RAW format, however,
 the original data can be used in special software* to adjust the image parameters
 (white balance, contrast, sharpness and saturation) making it possible to maintain
 the image quality while making changes. The resolution is fixed at 1856 x 1392.
 * The supplied driver software is required to open or adjust RAW images on a computer. Please see the
 separate Software Starter Guide.
 ** As measured by standard Canon test conditions.

Hello, I've been having major issues with my camera and the last sales representative I talked to in the store suggested getting help here. She thinks it's and issue with my data storage being full. Can you help tell if I'm looking at the correct manual and how we might be able to solve this issue?

session_1.speaker: assistant
session_1.text:
Certainly, I can help you troubleshoot your Canon PowerShot Pro90 IS. The document you've provided is indeed the correct User Guide for your camera model.

Let's start by diagnosing the "full data storage" issue. To do this effectively, I need to collect a few key details from you.

**Summary:** We will check if your camera's storage is full and guide you through the steps to free up space.

Please provide the following information:

1.  **CF Card:** What is the brand and storage size (e.g., 32MB, 64MB, 128MB) of your CompactFlash (CF) card?
2.  **Error Message/Code:** Is the camera displaying a specific error message or code on its screen? Common ones for storage issues are `CF Card Full` or a flashing number `0` for remaining images.
3.  **Steps Tried:** Have you already tried viewing and deleting images using the playback mode? Or have you tried formatting the card?
4.  **Accessories:** Are you using the original Canon battery pack (BP-511) or any other power source?
5.  **Environment:** Where are you currently using the camera (e.g., indoors, outdoors, hot/cold environment)?

Once you provide these details, I can give you specific, step-by-step instructions to resolve the issue.

session_1.speaker: user
session_1.text:
My CF Card is a  SanDisk CFexpress Card Type B 128mb
No there is no error code. It just keeps freezing on me when I try to take a picture
The nice lady at the store showed me how to delete a few videos of my dogs but says that from what she can see it seems to indicate a card error.
yes I'm using the original Canon battery pack (BP-511)
I use it in my apartment to take pictures of my Pomeranians to show my grand children when they come over. I'm told I keep my apartment very warm, but I find it cozy.
I do see a little red message here but the writing is so small I'm not sure what it's trying to tell me.

session_1.speaker: assistant
session_1.text:
Thank you for those details. That is very helpful information. I think I can identify the core issue now.

**Summary:** The primary problem is a significant incompatibility between your camera and the memory card you are using.

Let's break this down:

1.  **The Critical Issue: Wrong Card Type**
    Your Canon PowerShot Pro90 IS is designed to use **CompactFlash (CF) Type I or Type II cards**. The **SanDisk CFexpress Type B** card you have is a much newer, faster, and physically different type of card. They are not electrically compatible, even though they might look somewhat similar. Using an incompatible card is the most likely cause of the freezing and the suspected "card error."

2.  **The Red Message**
    The small red message is almost certainly an error code. This is a vital clue. To read it, please try the following:
    *   **Step 1:** Turn the main dial (the lower dial on the top-right) to the **Playback position** (the blue triangle symbol).
    *   **Step 2:** Look at the small **Display Panel** on the top of the camera (next to the viewfinder). The red error code should be showing there as a number or a short message.

    **Manual Reference:** *PowerShot Pro90 IS User Guide, "List of Error / Message Codes" (p. 126).*

    **Check:** Are you able to see and tell me what that red message says?

**Steps to Resolve the Issue:**

1.  **Power Down:** Turn the main dial to the **Off** position.
2.  **Remove the Incompatible Card:** Open the CF card slot cover on the right side of the camera and press the eject button to remove the CFexpress card.
3.  **Test the Camera Without a Card:**
    *   Turn the main dial back to the **Shooting** position (the red camera icon).
    *   Try to take a picture. The camera will use its small internal memory.
    *   **Check:** Does the camera still freeze, or does it operate normally now?

**Next Steps Based on Your Results:**

*   If the camera works **without** the card, the issue is 100% the incompatible CFexpress card. You will need to purchase a standard **CompactFlash (CF) card**. Given the age of the camera, a 128MB, 256MB, or 512MB card would be perfectly sufficient and readily available online.
*   If the camera **still freezes** without any card, the problem may be with the camera itself and would require professional service.

**Safety Preface:** Before purchasing a new CF card, please ensure the camera operates correctly without any card installed, as described in Step 3 above. This confirms the card is the issue.

Please let me know what the red error message says and if the camera works without the card. This will confirm the diagnosis and we can proceed from there.

Overview and Setup
The Whole Home Tri-Band WiFi 7 Mesh System creates dedicated high-speed WiFi 7
connections to your Internet service and provides three WiFi radios that operate
simultaneously:
• One 2.4 GHz radio that supports IEEE 802.11be with 1024-QAM for a throughput
of 688 Mbps
• One 5 GHz radio that support the new IEEE 802.11be standard with 4K-QAM and a
240 MHz channel width for a throughput of 8640 Mbps
• One 6 GHz radio that supports the new IEEE 802.11be standard with 4K-QAM and
a 320 MHz channel width for a throughput of 11520 Mbps
The new WiFi 7 features allow the Whole Home Tri-Band WiFi 7 Mesh System to provide
a total WiFi throughput of 21000 Mbps.
The Orbi router (model RBE871) connects to your modem or gateway. The Orbi satellite
(model RBE870) extends the WiFi 7 signal throughout your home.
This manual describes how to manage your Whole Home Tri-Band WiFi 7 Mesh System
from your Orbi router web interface. You can also manage your Orbi system from the
NETGEAR Orbi app.

What is WiFi 7?
WiFi 7, also known as IEEE 802.11be Extremely High Throughput (EHT), is a
next-generation WiFi standard. The new standard provides the capability for multi-gigabit
(multi-gig) WiFi throughout the home with faster speeds, less interference, and better
performance for high-bandwidth online activities.
New technologies in WiFi 7 provide the following benefits:
• 2.4 times faster speed than WiFi 6
• Double the maximum bandwidth for your devices
• Lower latency than WiFi 6
• A more reliable connection
For more information, visit the NETGEAR WiFi 7 page at
netgear.com/home/discover/wifi7.

Set up your satellite with a wired
connection to your router
Backhaul is a term for the communication performed between a mesh WiFi system's
router and its satellites. Instead of using a WiFi backhaul connection between the router
and the satellite, you can use a wired connection.
Set up and sync an Orbi satellite over a wired
connection
Your Orbi satellite automatically connects wirelessly to your Orbi router to create a
wireless backhaul. Your satellite and router also support Ethernet backhaul, which means
that you can use an Ethernet cable to connect your satellite to your router.
If your home has built-in Ethernet outlets in the rooms and the cables lead into the same
physical network, you can also connect both your Orbi router and Orbi satellite to the
Ethernet outlets and let them sync.
To set up and sync your Orbi satellite over a wired connection:
1. Place your satellite in the room where you want WiFi service.
2. Connect an Ethernet cable to a 2.5G Ethernet port on the satellite.

3. Connect the other end of the Ethernet cable to a 2.5G Ethernet LAN port on the
router.

The Power LED on the back of the satellite lights green.
The satellite LED pulses white. The satellite automatically syncs to the Orbi router.
NOTE: The first time that you sync the satellite and the router, the sync
process can take between five and ten minutes because the router might
automatically update the satellite’s firmware.
After the sync process is complete, the satellite LED lights blue for about three
minutes and then turns off. Blue indicates that the router and satellite successfully
synced and the wired connection between the router and satellite is good.

Connect to the network
You can connect to the Orbi network through a wired or WiFi connection. If you want
to connect on a computer using a static IP address, change the settings so that it uses
Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP).
Wired connection
You can connect your computer to the router using an Ethernet cable and join the
router’s local area network (LAN). The computer must have an Ethernet port.
To connect your computer to the router with an Ethernet cable:
1. Make sure that the router is receiving power (its Power LED is lit).
2. Connect an Ethernet cable to an Ethernet port on your computer.
3. Connect the other end of the Ethernet cable to one of the router’s Ethernet ports.
Your computer connects to the local area network (LAN). A message might display
on your computer screen to notify you that an Ethernet cable is connected.
WiFi connection
If you're installing your Orbi router for the first time, you can connect to the router's
WiFi network by scanning the QR code on your router with the camera app on your
mobile device. To scan the QR code with your camera app, your mobile device must
have iOS version 11 or later or Android version 10 or later.
You can also manually find and select the Orbi router's WiFi network from your
WiFi-enabled computer or mobile device.
To find and select the WiFi network:
1. Make sure that the router or satellite is receiving power (its Power LED is lit).

The WiFi network name is on the router label. The WiFi network name is the same
for the router and the satellite in the Orbi WiFi System.

WiFi network names are different. Use the router's WiFi network name during
initial setup.

• If you are not sure what type of IPv6 connection the router uses, use the Auto Detect
connection type, which lets the router detect the IPv6 type that is in use (see Use

an IPv6 6to4 tunnel Internet connection on page 38).
Specify Your Internet Settings 33 User Manual
Whole Home Tri-Band Mesh WiFi 7 System
When you enable IPv6 and select any connection type other than IPv6 pass-through,
the router starts the stateful packet inspection (SPI) firewall function on the WAN interface.
The router creates connection records and checks every inbound IPv6 packet. If the
router does not expect to receive such a packet, or the packet is not in the connection
record, the router blocks this packet.
Requirements for entering IPv6 addresses
IPv6 addresses are denoted by eight groups of hexadecimal quartets that are separated
by colons. You can reduce any four-digit group of zeros within an IPv6 address to a
single zero or omit it.
All of the following examples specify the same IPv6 address:
• 2001:db8:0000:0000:020f:24ff:febf:dbcb
• 2001:db8:0:0:20f:24ff:febf:dbcb
• 2001:db8::20f:24ff:febf:dbcb
• 2001:db8:0:0:20f:24ff:128.141.49.32
The following errors invalidate an IPv6 address:
• More than eight groups of hexadecimal quartets
• More than four hexadecimal characters in a quartet
• More than two colons in a row

Set up an IPv6 6rd tunnel Internet connection
The 6rd protocol makes it possible to deploy IPv6 to sites using a service provider’s
IPv4 network. 6rd uses the service provider’s own IPv6 address prefix. This limits the
operational domain of 6rd to the service provider’s network and is under direct control
of the service provider. The IPv6 service provided is equivalent to native IPv6. The 6rd
mechanism relies on an algorithmic mapping between the IPv6 and IPv4 addresses that
are assigned for use within the service provider’s network. This mapping allows for
Specify Your Internet Settings 44 User Manual

automatic determination of IPv4 tunnel endpoints from IPv6 prefixes, allowing stateless
operation of 6rd.
With a 6rd Tunnel configuration, the router follows the RFC5969 standard, supporting
two ways to establish a 6rd tunnel IPv6 WAN connection:
• Auto Detect Mode: In IPv6 Auto Detect mode, when the router receives option 212
from the DHCPv4 option, auto detect selects the IPv6 as 6rd Tunnel setting. The
router uses the 6rd option information to establish the 6rd connection.
• Manual Mode: Select 6rd. If the router receives option 212, the fields are
automatically completed. Otherwise, you must enter the 6rd settings.
